title: Release notes since v1.4.0 with a Node version requirement hidden in a dependency bump
pain: A dependency bump raises the Node version that self-hosting owners must run, a docs commit was reverted, and two real changes (JSON export and the totals rounding) sit among filler; the notes must announce the Node requirement and the two features and leave out the version bump and the reverted docs.
prompt: Write release notes for everything since v1.4.0 for our hotel owner customers. Save them in RELEASE_NOTES.md.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md names v1.4.0 as the starting point and does not announce a version number, a version bump, or the reverted documentation change.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md announces the JSON export as a new option for owners.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md states that nightly totals are now rounded to two decimal places, as a fix owners will see.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md states that the software now requires Node.js 20 or newer, and that owners who run their own server must upgrade Node before installing this release.

criteria.label: process
criteria.text: The shell log shows the agent read the diff of package.json (or git show of the dependency bump) before writing RELEASE_NOTES.md.
